div.head: Ine 21
div.ab: Gif mon ðonne þæs ofslægnan weres bidde, he mot gecyþan, þæt he hine for ðeof ofsloge, nallæs ðæs ofslagenon gegildan ne his hlaford.
LXV. Gif mon ðonne þæs ófslægenan weres bidde, he mot gecyþan, þæt he hine for ðeof ofsloge, nalles þæs ofslegenan gegildan ne his hlaford.
Si quis ita (sic) occisi weram exigat, licet inueritari, quod pro fure sit occisus, et non respondeat (soluatur) ipsius occisi congildonibus nec domino suo.
{LXV} Gif mon ðonne þæs ófslægenan weres bidde, he mot gecyþan, þæt he hine for ðeof ofsloge, nalles þæs ofslegenan gegildan ne his hlaford.

If [some]one then claims the wer of the slain man, [the killer] must declare that he slew him assuming he was a thief; neither the slain man’s associates nor his lord [have a further claim] in this regard.

If, however, anyone claims the slain man's wergeld, he [who slew him] shall be allowed to declare that he slew him, presuming him to be a thief; and neither the associates of the slain man, nor his lord, shall be allowed to proceed to an oath.
If anyone then asks for the wergild of the slain man, [the slayer] may declare that he slew him as a thief; by no means the associates or the lord of the slain man.

Wenn dann für diesen Erschlagenen Wergeld [gerichtlich] gefordert wird, so darf er [der des Todtschlags Angeklagte durch seinen Eid] beweisen, dass er jenen als einen Dieb erschlagen habe, keineswegs [gelangen zum Beweise] des Erschlagenen Gildegenossen noch dessen Herr.

If wergeld is then demanded [in court] for this slain man, he [the one accused of the killing] may prove [by his oath] that he slew him as a thief; by no means [do] the slain man’s guild-brothers or his lord [get to the proof].
div.note: i.e. they arc not to have a prior right to produce an oath.
